subject.title: Group reply pipeline silently drops agent-generated payload between turn completion and Telegram sendMessage

question: Should this issue stay open as the broader Telegram group reply-loss tracker after the stranded-final recovery PRs, or should maintainers make `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/85714` plus `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99536` the canonical remaining path?
rationale: Current main has partial mitigations and at least one open replacement PR, but the original issue combines Telegram group delivery, reaction failures, recipient normalization, and message-tool-only recovery, so automation should not choose the product boundary alone.

options.title: Keep Separate Until Live Telegram Proof
options.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer verifies the original Telegram group path on current main and decides whether any non-stranded-final failure remains.

options.title: Move To Stranded-Final Canonical Work
options.body: Treat the remaining actionable work as covered by `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/85714` and `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99536`, then close this only if Telegram-specific live proof shows no separate gap.

options.title: Split A Narrow Telegram Repro
options.body: Open or designate a narrower Telegram-only follow-up for reaction/recipient routing and close this broad report after linking the preserved evidence.

recommendation.title: Keep Separate Until Live Telegram Proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer verifies the original Telegram group path on current main and decides whether any non-stranded-final failure remains.

likelyOwner.reason: The central reply and Telegram dispatch history points to steipete as the strongest cross-surface routing owner for the product-boundary decision.
